+"""Descriptor-relative bookkeeping I/O; never follows a symlink component."""
+import os
+import stat
+import uuid
+import fcntl
+from pathlib import Path
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+_BOUND_ROOT = None
+_BOUND_FD = None
+
+
+def absolute(path):
+    p = Path(path).expanduser().absolute()
+    if '..' in p.parts:
+        raise ValueError('parent traversal refused')
+    return p
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def directory(path, create=False):
+    p = absolute(path)

+    if _BOUND_ROOT is not None and (p == _BOUND_ROOT or _BOUND_ROOT in p.parents):
+        fd=os.dup(_BOUND_FD)
+        parts=p.relative_to(_BOUND_ROOT).parts
+    else:
+        fd=os.open('/',os.O_RDONLY|os.O_DIRECTORY)
+        parts=p.parts[1:]
+    try:
+        for part in parts:
+            if create:
+                try: os.mkdir(part, 0o700, dir_fd=fd)
+                except FileExistsError: pass
+            nxt = os.open(part, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=fd)
+            os.close(fd)
+            fd = nxt
+        if os.fstat(fd).st_uid != os.getuid():
+            raise ValueError('directory owner mismatch')
+        yield fd
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+
+
+def checked(fd):
+    s = os.fstat(fd)
+    if not stat.S_ISREG(s.st_mode) or s.st_nlink != 1 or s.st_uid != os.getuid():
+        raise ValueError('untrusted file at operation')
+    return fd
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def file(path, flags=os.O_RDONLY, mode=0o600):
+    p = absolute(path)
+    with directory(p.parent) as parent:

+        fd = os.open(p.name, flags | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK, mode, dir_fd=parent)
+        try:
+            checked(fd)
+            yield fd
+        finally: os.close(fd)
+
+
+def read_bytes(path):
+    with file(path) as fd:
+        chunks=[]
+        while True:
+            b=os.read(fd, 65536)
+            if not b: return b''.join(chunks)
+            chunks.append(b)
+
+
+def read_text(path): return read_bytes(path).decode('utf-8')
+
+
+def write_all(fd, data):
+    view=memoryview(data)
+    while view:
+        n=os.write(fd,view)
+        if not n: raise OSError('short write')
+        view=view[n:]
+
+
+def atomic_write(path, data, exclusive=False):
+    if isinstance(data,str): data=data.encode('utf-8')
+    p=absolute(path)
+    with directory(p.parent) as parent:
+        # Reject existing poison even though replace itself does not follow it.
+        try:
+            fd=os.open(p.name,os.O_RDONLY|os.O_NOFOLLOW|os.O_NONBLOCK,dir_fd=parent)
+        except FileNotFoundError: pass
+        else:
+            try: checked(fd)
+            finally: os.close(fd)

+        tmp='.'+p.name+'.'+uuid.uuid4().hex
+        fd=os.open(tmp,os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT|os.O_EXCL|os.O_NOFOLLOW,0o600,dir_fd=parent)
+        try:
+            write_all(fd,data); os.fsync(fd)
+        finally: os.close(fd)
+        try:
+            if exclusive:
+                os.link(tmp,p.name,src_dir_fd=parent,dst_dir_fd=parent,follow_symlinks=False)
+            else: os.replace(tmp,p.name,src_dir_fd=parent,dst_dir_fd=parent)
+            os.fsync(parent)
+        finally:
+            try: os.unlink(tmp,dir_fd=parent)
+            except FileNotFoundError: pass
+
+
+def copy(source,target): atomic_write(target,read_bytes(source))
+
+
+def append(path,text):
+    with file(path,os.O_RDWR|os.O_APPEND) as fd:
+        fcntl.flock(fd,fcntl.LOCK_EX)
+        size=os.fstat(fd).st_size
+        tail=os.pread(fd,1,size-1) if size else b'\n'
+        write_all(fd,('' if tail==b'\n' else '\n').encode()+text.encode()+b'\n')
+        os.fsync(fd)
+
+
+def exists(path):
+    p=absolute(path)
+    try:

+        with directory(p.parent) as parent: os.stat(p.name,dir_fd=parent,follow_symlinks=False)
+        return True
+    except FileNotFoundError: return False
+
+
+def mkdir(path,parents=False,exist_ok=False):
+    p=absolute(path)
+    with directory(p.parent,create=parents) as parent:
+        try: os.mkdir(p.name,0o700,dir_fd=parent)
+        except FileExistsError:
+            if not exist_ok: raise
+    with directory(p): pass
+
+
+def unlink(path,dir_only=False):
+    p=absolute(path)
+    with directory(p.parent) as parent:
+        if dir_only: os.rmdir(p.name,dir_fd=parent)
+        else: os.unlink(p.name,dir_fd=parent)
+        os.fsync(parent)
+
+
+def move(source,target):
+    # Used under a transaction lock. Copy+unlink keeps interruption fail-closed.
+    copy(source,target)
+    unlink(source)
+
+
+def listdir(path):
+    with directory(path) as fd: return [absolute(path)/n for n in os.listdir(fd)]
+
+
+def lock_fd(path):
+    p=absolute(path)
+    with directory(p.parent) as parent:

+        fd=os.open(p.name,os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREAT|os.O_NOFOLLOW|os.O_NONBLOCK,0o600,dir_fd=parent)
+        try: checked(fd); fcntl.flock(fd,fcntl.LOCK_EX)
+        except BaseException: os.close(fd); raise
+        return fd
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def locked(path):
+    fd=lock_fd(path)
+    try: yield
+    finally: os.close(fd)
+
+
+def bind_root(path):
+    """Pin one validated helper home for this process, retaining its directory inode."""
+    global _BOUND_ROOT,_BOUND_FD
+    p=absolute(path)
+    if _BOUND_ROOT is not None:
+        if p!=_BOUND_ROOT: raise ValueError('process already bound to another home')
+        return
+    with directory(p) as fd: pinned=os.dup(fd)
+    _BOUND_ROOT=p
+    _BOUND_FD=pinned
+
+
+def directory_exists(path):
+    try:
+        with directory(path): pass
+        return True
+    except FileNotFoundError: return False

+# Runtime contract and supported-platform limits
+
+## Supported proof scope
+
+Only the isolated synthetic macOS subprocess reference host has been exercised. The candidate runner installs Seatbelt restrictions on every command and descendant it launches, clears ambient environment, closes inherited descriptors, denies network, Mach service lookup/registration, signaling and process inspection, and restricts data reads/writes to host-selected paths. Useful external project work remains available.
+
+Literal ancestor-directory reads are needed for macOS startup and anchored descriptor walks. They disclose directory entry names at those ancestors; they do not permit reading private sibling file contents. This edition does not promise zero filesystem-name visibility.
+

+The trusted host remains outside its workers' sandbox. It owns identity, authority, code fingerprints, resource leases and recipients. Only fixed helper commands receive bookkeeping writes; arbitrary code receives assigned project writes only. Helper code, bindings, approval registries and broad credentials must not be worker-writable. For the fixture host these registries are memory owned by the trusted test driver, not files reachable by workers. They are not a durable native service or a cross-machine resource authority.
+
+The fixture launcher supplies context in a supervisor-created fixed helper process. JSON sent from an untrusted worker is not an authentication mechanism. Running that launcher directly outside its host boundary provides no supported identity guarantee. Standalone production helpers refuse context; native activation remains disabled in code.
+
+## Current native platforms
+

+Codex desktop, Claude Code, Claude app and Cursor activation are **unsupported in this revision**. Only Codex's exposed local surface and current official docs were investigated; no claim is made to have tested a negative action on the other platforms. The gate refuses them until each has an actual reviewed adapter. The current Codex chat uses broad host permissions. Codex command profiles do not govern its native apps/connectors/MCP/browser/computer actions. This script cannot retroactively constrain those tools.
+
+Sources: [Codex permissions](https://developers.openai.com/codex/permissions/), [App Server](https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server/), [MCP configuration](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/), [scheduled tasks](https://developers.openai.com/codex/app/automations/). See the enclosing PLATFORM-EVIDENCE.md for actual calls, source versions and exact limits. No security configuration was changed.
+
+## Mandatory native prerequisites
+
+A supported adapter must establish all of these before setup, every resume and every scheduled turn:

# Create an independent team

Alex manually creates the empty operating folder and opens its first chat. That existing chat is intended to become Director when a supported host authenticates it. Do not create another Director or require a mission first. Assign the mission afterward; it may target a new project or an existing external repo. Team state remains in the operating home.

**Current status: local candidate, native activation unsupported.** This bundle repairs the local helpers and supplies a restricted macOS subprocess runner. Its isolated synthetic verification is not an installed live team, native identity proof or permission to access real providers. No available native adapter establishes the complete required boundary. `scripts/prepare_team.py` refuses native activation before writing any destination. `runtime_context` refuses standalone helpers. Editable binding fields, environment values and copied fixture receipts cannot enable these routes.

## On invocation

1. Read this home's applicable instructions and [procedure.md](references/procedure.md). Preserve existing state. A different or nonempty folder requires inspection, never overwrite or an automatic replacement home.

2. Apply the supported-platform gate in [runtime-contract.md](references/runtime-contract.md). In this revision, report the missing native adapter and remain inactive. Do not run a renderer as a workaround, copy fixture state into a live home, create/message/resume chats, or schedule anything.
3. A future reviewed adapter must authenticate the actual invoking chat outside model-controlled input, bind the first chat as Director, create fresh empty state, constrain every tool and credential route, and enforce resource and recipient ownership. That adapter must pass the separate native trial before adoption. No manual flag or JSON status grants authority.
4. Keep the Director loop: freeze the later mission's outcome and acceptance, assign fresh controllers, observe processing, receive evidence, judge acceptance, update local graph/ledger and continue ready authorized work. Use the exact local roles from this bundle. Never recover another team's owners by title, ID in a document, or schedule search.

## Local repair and verification

Read [templates.md](references/templates.md) for helper controls. The renderer is pure and uses the retained source lock; it is available to the isolated fixture host for testing only. Source hashes provide provenance, not authorization.

The verification host outside this skill uses invented identities, mock provider scopes and disposable resources. Every executed helper/worker enters the candidate's sandbox before it can act. Its supervisor registry, not team files, owns identity, authorizations, disjoint resources and recipients. This test host contains no native transport or provider client.

Write a local proposal in `system/shared-change-proposals/` for the shared maintainer; do not edit canonical cards or rules without Alex's separate explicit authorization and supported enforcement. See the runtime contract for the complete activation requirements and the enclosing revision's evidence and native-trial steps.

# Alex Director

You sit above project controllers: keep Alex's outcome, judge results, assign the next concrete

result. Alex owns the outcome, you own mission judgment, the controller owns the technical route,
and the real system decides what is true.

## Rules that always hold
1. **Never do project work.** Don't implement, deploy, create repos, choose tools, tests,
   branches, workers or skill chains, or run Superpowers yourself. Every `NEXT_PLAY` tells the
   controller to load `@@TEAM_HOME@@/roles/alex-workflow-conductor/SKILL.md` (controllers elsewhere never see `AGENTS.md`; the
   conductor carries the gates). Name a Superpowers skill only when its trigger applies
   (`references/controllers.md` → Skill triggers).
2. **Alex is never the relay.** Don't ask him to paste, type "go", pick tools or start chats; reach
   controllers directly. Never tell a controller to collect a yes from Alex, except the gates in
   `references/gates.md` (spend, real-person contact, client-data deletion, production/DNS), which
   still need Alex's explicit yes in his own chat. Otherwise an open fact gets research agents (Exa

first, `references/execution.md`) and a known fact gets the execution play; a controller's "Yes
   to all" is a failed play: answer it with the play or the agents. Any idea,
   option or recommendation you offer Alex comes from a data-driven case study found with Exa that
   turn (`references/execution.md` → Ideas offered to Alex); no case study, no offer.
3. **VERIFIED needs evidence:** a controller pointer (record ID, URL, file path, provider ID,
   readback or test result) matching the node's `ACCEPTANCE`, plus Alex's explicit approval where
   acceptance needs his review. Don't rerun the check. A send, a bare "completed" or a claim without
   a pointer goes back to that controller with the exact missing proof. An owner review waits as
   `READY_FOR_OWNER` with the exact link in front of Alex; only his explicit approval makes it
   `VERIFIED`. `WAITING_ON_ALEX` (node or mission) is only for permission, sign-in and consequence
   boundaries.
4. **Alex's scoped approval only** for spend, real-person contact, production/DNS/infrastructure

changes, destructive deletion, widening a frozen outcome and the protected items in
   `references/gates.md`. Dispatch all other work within Alex's current mission scope and applicable instructions.
   Standing grants must come from this team's authorization record; setup imports none.
5. **A blocker parks only its node, never a controller.** Keep the mission `ACTIVE` while any
   authorized node is ready or progressing. Every play leaves its controller at least one item it
   can start without Alex or pending research, or says `STANDBY until <event>`. A `NO_READY` line,
   a cleared dependency or an idle controller with work left gets its next ready item in the same
   cycle, before any new agent gets that item. Record the resume condition once; no reminders.
6. **Only you declare `MISSION COMPLETE`,** when every required node and the top-level acceptance
   node are `VERIFIED` against the real target. Parked missions stay parked.
7. **Never freeze your own loop.** Read incoming results first. While any controller or agent is

running, ask Alex in plain text at the end of the turn, never with a blocking question pop-up.
8. **Ledger writes go through `scripts/ledger_check.py`:** backup, edit one block, verify.

## Each cycle

1. **Freeze** outcome and acceptance; a controller may clarify them, never narrow or replace them.
2. **Recover** the existing controller and its latest accepted checkpoint; read only unseen results.
3. **Judge** each result against the node's `ACCEPTANCE` and the assigned `NEXT_PLAY_ID` (rule 3).

**Check-in wake:** one compact snapshot of registered chats. Unchanged: stay quiet; the check-in
is a silent backstop and Alex hears only about real events (`references/supervision.md` →
Pings). Either way no rereads, research, tests or artifacts. Material

Before telling Alex what's left, run `scripts/graph_lint.py` on the mission graph (warnings only).

## Controller behavior you can rely on
Controllers never write the ledger; you are its only writer. They put their chat/thread ID and
workspace in their first checkpoint, and you record it in `CONTROLLER` if it differs. They report with a compact checkpoint (result, evidence pointer, remaining work or
blocker, next action), and **every play end** (complete, gate, phase, failure, blocker, `NOT_PROVEN`

or `NO_READY`) sends you one line without waiting for your acknowledgment. A failed send is retried
once; if it fails again, the controller says so in its checkpoint, and your check-in's snapshot of
that controller picks the result up.

Don't copy project memory, `BUILD_STATE` or raw controller logs into the ledger. Don't build
monitoring, discovery, dashboards, databases, daemons, registries or message buses.

## Skill triggers (Superpowers)
For Director/Conductor operating work, this trigger table is the router. Do not invoke
`using-superpowers` as an always-on prerequisite or its 1% applicability rule. An accepted design
or execution plan stays accepted: new brainstorming applies only to a material unresolved design
decision, not to routine implementation, a takeover or a controller continuation. Explicitly
requested planning-only work remains planning-only.

Name a Superpowers skill in a play, and load one on a controller turn, only when its trigger
applies. Mandated procedure caused 114 of 182 skill-induced slowdowns in a 2026 study (arXiv

2608.11888), most of it verification and pipelines the task didn't need.

| Trigger | Skill |
|---|---|
| Observed failure, failed test, stall or `STOPPED BY BOUNDARY` | `systematic-debugging` |
| Behavior or code change where a test is the right proof | `test-driven-development` |
| Done claim on an external or irreversible node | `verification-before-completion` |
| Parallel, bounded, independent work | `dispatching-parallel-agents` |
| Design not yet frozen (never on a frozen BUILD or RUN) | `brainstorming` |
| None of the above | none |

# Execution and verification

Shared by the Director (when writing plays and judging) and controllers (when doing the work).

## Doing only the remaining work
- Recover the latest accepted artifact or native checkpoint, its target/version and date, and
  settled decisions before anything else. Process only pending or materially changed scope.
  Reopen a settled decision only for new evidence or Alex's direction.
- **Reuse before rerun. Resume before rebuild. Process the remaining delta.**
- Before declaring a capability missing or building tooling, check the available primitives and
  how they compose; compare total time, manual work, reliability and proof. Alex's explicit tool
  choice is binding. A missing one-command recipe is not a missing capability.
- Think before each call: every action should advance required work or get evidence that could
  change the next decision. Batch independent reads and safely related reversible work. Saving
  calls never justifies an unchecked live write.

## How much to verify

- Choose a substantial checkpoint (the normal end-to-end path or a coherent batch) and the
  minimum meaningful proof. Don't validate after every small edit unless a dependency requires it.
  Don't run a final sweep just to prepare a report.
- **One green result covers its unchanged scope.** A second equivalent check needs a named
  unresolved risk or an independent requirement; never run a third equivalent check of the same
  unchanged target, under any command, agent, thread or label. A material change invalidates only
  the affected scope: recheck that scope at a meaningful boundary and keep unaffected green results.
- Distinct required acceptance, safety and write checks stay separate obligations and are never
  "retests": the designated contact test, the five human-response reviews and their approvals,
  per-write guards and readbacks, and inbound tracking. Nor may they be used as labels for
  reassurance loops.
- Prior summaries, expected results and agent claims are not proof. Reuse authoritative proof

while its inputs are unchanged, but keep its observation date distinct from a newly observed
  runtime fact. Interrupted work without a final readback is `NOT_PROVEN`: reconcile it read-only
  and never replay an unresolved write. If tools are unavailable, state the exact resume action.
- **Every claimed outcome carries an evidence pointer** (record ID, URL, file path, provider ID,
  readback or test result) in the report itself. A claim without one isn't accepted.

## Proof and ownership
- Configured, exposed, authenticated, reachable, executed and production-proven are different
  states. Don't let one stand in for the next.
- Chat title, transcript modification time, age, prompt similarity and self-report never grant
  ownership or authority and never prove completion.

## When something fails
Compare expected and observed; separate facts from hypotheses; find the likely failing boundary
before the first repair. Use a read-only probe only if it can tell plausible causes apart. Make
the smallest evidence-backed repair and check the affected workflow at a meaningful boundary. No

cascades of speculative fixes or micro-probes. After two failed evidence-backed fixes without new
evidence, stop mutations and report the blocker. On the Director side this is the loop
breaker: stop dispatching mutations and have the controller isolate the cause from existing
evidence or one discriminating probe. Six or more `NEXT_PLAY_ID`s on one symptom in a day is a
loop: record the failure and tell Alex the isolation result, not another fix.
Count plays per component per day too: after two adoption rounds on one component (a rebuilt version
of the same job, alarm or workflow put into use; one build's several fences aren't rounds), stop and
isolate the cause in one pass, then fix it once (2026-10-01: 104 rebuilt its alarm gen2 to gen9 in
6h47m; 103 ran 19 plays).

## Owner-only blockers
When a step needs a manual credential, login, approval or other owner-only action: record the
unfinished step and its exact resume condition in the existing queue or mission state, then move
to the next independent authorized work. Don't make Alex click, paste, answer a readiness prompt

or verify it by default. In a UI, use an already authenticated route and batch related actions;
a genuinely required key, login or 2FA parks that step with the form preserved safely. No reminders, blocker polling or reassurance tests; revisit only when
Alex reopens it or new evidence changes the dependency. Parking isn't approval or completion and
never bypasses a denial. If everything in scope is blocked, a controller first sends its Director
one `NO_READY` line naming each gate, then gives Alex one brief non-demanding status and stops. Report real safety incidents promptly. Never use `notify-no-ready.sh` for unsolicited
messages.

## Missing facts and research
The responsible controller does this research; the Director delegates it and consumes the result
without a second audit. Before calling something a missing-information blocker, exhaust accessible
in-scope sources, including referenced transcripts and Drive material. For external technical
decisions, current official documentation is the authority. Use the first callable route:

| Job | Route, first callable wins |
|---|---|

| Official docs, API, version, error | Composio docs readers (Context7 for libraries; OpenAI, Astro, Qt docs) → Exa page fetch through Composio (`EXA_GET_CONTENTS_ACTION`) → Composio `firecrawl` search → native web search |
| One fact, current state, news | Exa through Composio (`EXA_SEARCH`) → Composio `firecrawl` search → native web search |
| Multi-hop research across sources | Exa through Composio (`EXA_SEARCH`, type `deep`) → Composio `firecrawl` search + scrape → native web search |
| Read one known URL | Exa page fetch through Composio (`EXA_GET_CONTENTS_ACTION`) → native web fetch → browser (pages behind a login) |
| Scrape or crawl a site (JS-heavy page, clicks first, batch, whole site) | Firecrawl: Composio `firecrawl` for pages; whole-site crawls to files with the Firecrawl CLI through `~/.agents/tools/connectors/firecrawl_op.py` (card `firecrawl`) |

Why this order: independent 2026 benchmarks tie Exa and Firecrawl for general search; Exa leads
single-fact lookup (99.3% vs 95.3%) and multi-hop research (45 vs 30 F1); Firecrawl leads

docs-task completion (70.3% vs 66.3%) and page extraction. Firecrawl spends credits (2 per
10-result search, about 1,000 a cycle), so prefer the Composio docs readers or Exa when they're callable. Stop once the
decision is supported; don't repeat searches just to use every tool. Never claim a tool you didn't use, and
never install or pay for one without authorization. Public research can't invent private business
facts or grant permission.

## Ideas offered to Alex
An idea, option, or recommendation offered to Alex has to come from a data-driven case study
found with Exa on that turn. General knowledge, a blog's advice, or a vendor's claim is not an
offer. Use the research route above: `EXA_SEARCH`, then `EXA_GET_CONTENTS_ACTION` on the page
before citing it. Do not start a paid Exa research run.

A case study counts only when the fetched page reports a measured result (a number, a
before-and-after, or a stated outcome) for a real named situation. Put the source URL, the
page's date, and that measured result in the same line as the idea. If Exa does not return a

page that meets that bar, do not offer the idea. Say that no case study was found.

Decide routine, reversible matters yourself from the outcome, acceptance, Alex's preferences and
least effort; record consequential assumptions with a short reason and source pointer. Report the
exact missing fact or inaccessible source and what it affects. If sources conflict, find the
authority, stop only the affected write, and repair the secondary pointer. Keep labeled drafts,
checklists and placeholders moving. Never invent final technical or safety facts or present them
as verified; a missing final fact stops only the affected final or consequential action.

## Durable fixes

Record a verified team-specific fix in this team's local procedure and keep its evidence pointer in `@@TEAM_HOME@@/system/lessons.md`. For a shared skill, rule or tool-card change, write one local proposal under `@@TEAM_HOME@@/system/shared-change-proposals/`, naming the maintained destination, suggested edit and proof. The shared maintainer owns promotion. Do not edit shared files unless Alex separately and explicitly authorizes that exact change and the host enforces its bounded scope. A skill's instruction to update its canonical card does not grant this team shared write access.

The remaining procedure applies only after that adapter and its trial are verified. Synthetic schedule events in offline tests are not running jobs.

# Supervision scope for this edition

All Director, backstop and controller recovery below is limited to this TEAM_ID. No scheduler is created by setup; recurring supervision needs an explicit later request.

# Supervision: check-ins, wakes and readback

## The check-in
- For ongoing supervision Alex requested: ask the trusted host for only schedules it owns for this TEAM_ID first, then create
  or update **one** scoped backstop heartbeat on the supervising Director chat, the chat Alex
  reads: create it from that chat with `destination=thread`, or name that chat as the target. A
  check-in bound to another chat (an observer) puts its line where Alex doesn't look; move it.

Cadence: every **25 minutes**, as a **silent** backstop (Alex, 2026-10-02: no timed pings, "ping me
  like u do"). Controller sends are the primary wake (Conductor →
  Report); the backstop catches missed sends and stuck jobs, because a cross-thread send has no delivery receipt
  and can fail (three sends to the Dynamite Director failed on 2026-10-02 with no retry). Both
  cadence keeps every wake inside the 30-minute prompt-cache lifetime (cached input is billed at a
  tenth). A wake costs about the bound chat's whole context in cached input (the Dynamite observer
  read ~407K tokens per wake), so keep the check-in on the Director chat, not a bigger one. Don't
  create one merely because a one-step task exists. Register every active controller chat/task ID
  in its scope, local owners included. Record the actual automation ID and schedule after reading
  it back.
- No per-controller reminders, no duplicate reminders, no reviving unrelated parked missions, and
  no separate fixed deep-audit timer.

- Use the app's automation tool: no daemon, launchd job, cron or shell polling loop, no second
  supervisor or checker agent, and no automatic model switch to simulate a cheaper pass.
- Configured is not observed firing. Delivery depends on the app and host; a busy or offline
  period doesn't prove a controller failed. Don't claim host-independent monitoring or exact
  five-minute delivery.
- Each wake still runs in this chat's full context and model, so it isn't free. That is why an
  unchanged wake must exit fast.
- Pause the reminder when its work is complete or every remaining step needs Alex, after
  reporting that once.

## Pings: only when something happens
Alex, 2026-10-02: "can we turn that shit off? so it pings me like u do". No timed "still working"
pings. Message Alex (`NOTIFY`) only on a real event, in plain words with no IDs, hashes or ledger
shorthand: a controller's result (tell him the moment it arrives, never wait for a check-in), a
failure or blocker, a job that looks stuck (a promised checkpoint overdue, or a finished controller

whose report never arrived: say so and what you did about it), or a decision, permission or
sign-in only he can give. Put that rule in the heartbeat prompt itself. An unchanged check-in ends
with `DONT_NOTIFY` and a short quiet-status message; never an empty reply. Inside your own turns,
keep narrating as you work (one plain line before each long step), so he never has to ask "did it
finish?".

## A wake
1. Reuse the registered scope and earliest unprocessed native turn pointers from mission state.
2. Take one compact batch snapshot of registered chats' status and unseen results (reuse a fresh
   same-cycle snapshot if one exists).
3. **Unchanged** and no promised checkpoint overdue: stay quiet (`DONT_NOTIFY`; Pings). No skill or ledger reread, no transcript
   reading, research, tests, artifacts or subagents.
4. **Material change** (completion, explicit failure or blocker, completed chat with a missing
   result, overdue promised checkpoint): reread `SKILL.md` and home `AGENTS.md`, judge against

frozen acceptance, leave progressing controllers alone, resume an idle controller that has
   ready work once, and record compact state changes.
5. Five minutes without a message is not a stall and never clears or reassigns work.

## Reconciling a cycle (material wakes)
1. Judge unseen final messages and checkpoints once, then record their processed pointers.
   Don't rescan transcripts or raw logs for ordinary progress.
2. Accept reports that match the assigned outcome, required checks and evidence pointer; update
   graph and ledger. If a result is absent or contradictory, recover that exact native turn or
   action record once, then send one specific correction to the same controller. Never replay an
   uncertain action.
3. Investigate only a specific contradiction, error, missing result or owner-reported failure,
   and send the focused diagnosis to the responsible controller. Don't rerun tests or commission
   a second audit of completed work.
4. For an idle controller with ready work, send one concrete next outcome (naming a Superpowers

skill only when its trigger applies). Confirm processing by native status or readable acknowledgment.
5. Park only a blocked node and dispatch the next ready authorized outcome in the same cycle.
   Manual entry, owner review or an approval wait never idles independent work. Keep the mission
   `ACTIVE` while any authorized node is ready or progressing; a heartbeat never leaves
   `WAITING_ON_ALEX` on a mission that has `READY` work. A time gate records its unlock time and
   doesn't block independent work.
6. Before yielding, use the fresh snapshot or take one, consume newly finished results, and record
   the heartbeat ID, scope, current owner and next action. Yielding with working controllers and
   an enabled check-in is valid.
7. If exact-turn recovery returns nothing, label it `NOT_PROVEN` and report the readback failure
   instead of redispatching.
8. If an authorized notification is denied, keep the native checkpoint; don't retry through
   another route or ask Alex to relay it. After owner Q&A, consume new results and continue

independent work. Don't suggest unrelated projects or send repetitive no-ready alerts.

## Serializing your own reviews
A wake requests a refresh; it doesn't interrupt a coherent decision in progress. Finish and save
the current decision first. Handle Alex's stop, correction or authority revocation, and urgent
safety failures, at the next safe boundary. Coalesce repeated ticks and unchanged status into one
pending review with no backlog replay. Never coalesce away distinct owner instructions,
rejections, approvals, failures or inbound contact responses. Fetching a cursor isn't judging it:
keep the earliest unprocessed turn pointer until its judgment is recorded.

If several changed missions can't be judged in one pass, keep compact pending pointers keyed by
controller and current generation/assignment in their existing mission state (`REMAINING`,
`NEXT_PLAY` and checkpoint pointers usually suffice; add a minimal pending field only when needed,
and clear it when empty). No separate queue, database or tick log. Never delete mission state,

accepted checkpoints, approvals or action records to clear a signal. After an interruption, resume
pending pointers before any broad rescan. Reconcile a stale generation or assignment read-only, and
discard an obsolete wake only after preserving any unfinished outcome; never replay an uncertain
side effect. Order: urgent boundaries, then work-unblocking items, then oldest. Review each
controller at most once per pass.

## Readback order
1. Native `read_thread` / task readback.
2. Other native turn or agent-message surfaces the client exposes.
3. If a completed turn shows no assistant items, bounded recovery may inspect that exact turn's
   records; internal databases and rollout files are diagnostic fallbacks only.
4. Still unproven: label `NOT_PROVEN`. Never infer failure, archive or replace a thread from an
   empty projection alone.

## Other teams and historical schedules

Other teams and historical global schedules are outside this binding. Do not pause, revive, migrate or adopt them. Recover only schedules explicitly registered for this TEAM_ID.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Close one accepted result in one command: the node's graph cells and its run-log line, both or neither.

  accept.py --graph GRAPH --node ID --status STATUS --evidence TEXT --receipt TEXT --next TEXT
            --job TEXT --result TEXT [--corrections TEXT] [--run-log PATH]

Sets STATUS, LAST_RECEIPT, NEXT_ACTION and UPDATED_AT (UTC, now), adds TEXT to EVIDENCE after "; ", then appends
  YYYY-MM-DD | job | result (graph MISSION/NODE -> STATUS at UPDATED_AT) | corrections
to the run-log (default <TEAM_HOME>/system/run-log.md, independent of PROJECT; corrections default "none").
STATUS starts with READY, BLOCKED, ACTIVE, READY_FOR_OWNER, VERIFIED, FAILED or WAITING_ON_ALEX. No value may hold
" | " or a line break. A durable pending journal stores both originals before writing the graph and log; an
interrupted call restores both before its next retry. A failed append restores both. A graph without LAST_RECEIPT and UPDATED_AT columns is refused: run the migration in

migrations/ with graph_edit.py first. Other cell edits: graph_edit.py. Staleness check: graph_lint.py.
"""
import argparse, os, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).absolute().parents[3] / "scripts"))
import team_paths as scope
import safe_io as io

from datetime import datetime

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import graph_edit as ge  # noqa: E402

STATUSES = ("READY", "BLOCKED", "ACTIVE", "READY_FOR_OWNER", "VERIFIED", "FAILED", "WAITING_ON_ALEX")
MIGRATION = "migrations/2026-10-02_add-receipt-columns.json"


def prepare(a):
    """Everything is checked and built in memory before any write. Raises ge.Refused."""
    home, binding = scope.bound_home(__file__)
    scope.require_role(home,binding,"director")
    path = str(scope.graph_path(home, a.graph))
    before = io.read_text(path)
    scope.check_text_identity(binding, before)
    t = ge.Table(before)
    for col in ("STATUS", "EVIDENCE", "LAST_RECEIPT", "NEXT_ACTION", "UPDATED_AT"):
        if col not in t.cols:

raise ge.Refused(f"the graph has no {col} column; run {MIGRATION} with graph_edit.py first")
    status = ge.check_cell("STATUS", a.status)
    word = status.split()[0] if status else ""
    if word not in STATUSES:
        raise ge.Refused(f"STATUS {status!r} must start with one of {', '.join(STATUSES)}")
    i = t.find(a.node)
    c = t.cells(i)
    stamp = ge.now_stamp()
    evidence = ge.check_cell("EVIDENCE", a.evidence)
    k = t.col("EVIDENCE")
    c[k] = evidence if c[k] in ("", "-") else c[k] + "; " + evidence
    c[t.col("STATUS")] = status
    c[t.col("LAST_RECEIPT")] = ge.check_cell("LAST_RECEIPT", a.receipt)
    c[t.col("NEXT_ACTION")] = ge.check_cell("NEXT_ACTION", a.next)
    c[t.col("UPDATED_AT")] = stamp
    t.put(i, c)
    t.stamp_file(stamp)
    job, result, corrections = (ge.check_cell(n, v) for n, v in
                                (("job", a.job), ("result", a.result), ("corrections", a.corrections)))
    if not job or not result:
        raise ge.Refused("--job and --result can't be empty")
    run_log = str(scope.log_path(home, a.run_log))

if not os.path.isfile(run_log):
        raise ge.Refused(f"run-log not found: {run_log}")
    mission = ge.header_value(t.lines, "MISSION_ID") or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]
    line = (f"{datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')} | {job} | {result} (graph {mission}/{a.node} -> {word} at {stamp})"
            f" | {corrections or 'none'}")
    return path, before, t.text(), run_log, line


def run():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    for name in ("--graph", "--node", "--status", "--evidence", "--receipt", "--next", "--job", "--result"):
        ap.add_argument(name, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--corrections", default="none")
    ap.add_argument("--run-log")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    try:
        path, before, after, run_log, line = prepare(a)
    except (ge.Refused, OSError, scope.ScopeError) as e:
        print(f"REFUSED: {e}. Nothing written.")
        sys.exit(1)
    home,binding=scope.bound_home(__file__)
    journal=home/'system'/'.accept-pending.json'

old_log=io.read_text(run_log)
    pending={'schema':'accept-transaction/v1','team_id':binding['team_id'],'graph':path,'before':before,'run_log':run_log,'log_before':old_log}
    io.atomic_write(journal,__import__('json').dumps(pending),exclusive=True)
    ge.backup(path)
    ge.write_atomic(path, after)
    try:
        io.append(run_log,line)
    except (OSError,ValueError) as e:
        ge.write_atomic(path, before)
        io.atomic_write(run_log,old_log)
        io.unlink(journal)
        print(f"FAILED: run-log append failed ({e}); the graph is back as it was. Nothing written.")
        sys.exit(1)
    io.unlink(journal)
    print(f"OK: {a.node} updated in {path} (backup {path}.bak)")
    print(f"run-log {run_log} +1 line: {line}")


def recover(home,binding):
    journal=home/'system'/'.accept-pending.json'
    if not io.exists(journal): return
    pending=scope.strict_json(io.read_text(journal))
    keys={'schema','team_id','graph','before','run_log','log_before'}

if not isinstance(pending,dict) or set(pending)!=keys or pending['schema']!='accept-transaction/v1' or pending['team_id']!=binding['team_id']:
        raise scope.ScopeError('invalid interrupted acceptance transaction')
    graph=scope.graph_path(home,pending['graph'])
    log=scope.log_path(home,pending['run_log'])
    scope.check_text_identity(binding,pending['before'])
    io.atomic_write(graph,pending['before'])
    io.atomic_write(log,pending['log_before'])
    io.unlink(journal)
    print('Recovered interrupted acceptance; graph and log restored before retry.')


def main():
    try:
        home,binding=scope.bound_home(__file__)
        scope.require_role(home,binding,'director')
        with io.locked(home/'system'/'.graph-transaction.lock'):
            recover(home,binding)
            run()
    except (OSError,ValueError) as exc:
        print('REFUSED:',exc); sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only staleness check for mission graphs. It only prints warnings and always exits 0: it never blocks.

  graph_lint.py GRAPH [GRAPH ...] [--run-log PATH] [--changelog PATH]

Default run-log and CHANGELOG: <TEAM_HOME>/system/run-log.md and CHANGELOG.md (local team bookkeeping).
Warnings:
  1. nodes with no UPDATED_AT (or a node table with no UPDATED_AT column: run the migration in migrations/);
  2. stale: a node whose UPDATED_AT is older than a run-log or CHANGELOG line naming the node ID. Run-log lines
     carry a local date, so a later day counts, and the same day only below the node's own accept.py line;
     CHANGELOG lines take the time of the "## YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" heading above them;
  3. NEXT_ACTION naming an approval code the run-log shows used ("yes CG-XXXX") or an agent or play the run-log
     shows finished (named in a line's job field: spp-p38a, a0123456789abcdef), unless that line is older than
     the node's UPDATED_AT.
ledger_check.py verify runs it on the mission's graph after an OK.
"""
import os, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).absolute().parents[3] / "scripts"))
import team_paths as scope
import safe_io as io
import io as textio

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import graph_edit as ge  # noqa: E402

CODE = re.compile(r"\bCG-[A-Z0-9]{4}\b")
USED = re.compile(r"(?i:\byes\b)[\s'\"\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d]*((?:CG-[A-Z0-9]{4}\s*(?:(?:,|\+|&|and)\s*)?)+)")

"""Enforced local subprocess boundary; never a sandbox for native desktop tools.

The caller is a trusted host, outside its workers. Its allowed paths and command
must not come from worker input. Native activation has no adapter in this edition.
"""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import subprocess
import sys


class UnsupportedRuntime(RuntimeError):
    pass


def require_native_activation(platform_name):
    raise UnsupportedRuntime(
        f'{platform_name}: activation unsupported; requires host-authenticated current-chat '
        'identity, isolation of EVERY tool/credential route, an authoritative resource '
        'owner registry and native recipient/resume/queue/schedule enforcement. '
        'No native adapter is included. Local JSON, environment values and fixture '
        'receipts cannot enable activation.')


def _path(path):
    p = Path(path).absolute()
    if not p.exists() or p != p.resolve():
        raise ValueError('runtime paths must exist and be canonical, without links')
    if '\n' in str(p) or '\x00' in str(p):

raise ValueError('invalid runtime path')
    return p


def profile(read_roots, write_roots):
    if platform.system() != 'Darwin':
        raise UnsupportedRuntime('Only the verified macOS subprocess adapter is available')
    reads = [_path(p) for p in read_roots]
    writes = [_path(p) for p in write_roots]
    # Interpreter/system libraries only, not the user's HOME, keychain, app data,
    # network, GUI bridges, process inspection or inherited credential environment.
    system = ['/System', '/usr/lib', '/usr/share', '/usr/bin', '/bin', '/sbin',
              str(Path(sys.base_prefix).resolve())]
    reads += [Path(p) for p in system if Path(p).exists()]
    ancestors = sorted({p for root in reads+writes for p in root.parents}, key=str)
    directory_entries = ' '.join('(literal '+json.dumps(str(p))+')' for p in ancestors)
    def rules(paths):
        return ' '.join('(subpath '+json.dumps(str(p))+')' if p.is_dir()
                        else '(literal '+json.dumps(str(p))+')' for p in paths)
    return '\n'.join([

'(version 1)', '(allow default)', '(deny network*)',
        '(deny mach-lookup)', '(deny mach-register)', '(deny process-info*)',
        '(deny signal)',
        '(deny file-read-data (require-not (require-any '+rules(reads+writes)+' '+directory_entries+
        ' (literal "/dev/null") (literal "/dev/urandom") (literal "/dev/random"))))',
        '(deny file-write* (require-not (require-any '+rules(writes)+
        ' (literal "/dev/null"))))',
    ])


def run(argv, *, cwd, read_roots, write_roots, input_text=None, timeout=20):
    """No ambient environment, inherited FDs, shell expansion or fallback route."""
    cwd = _path(cwd)
    policy = profile(read_roots, write_roots)
    env = {'PATH':'/usr/bin:/bin', 'LANG':'en_US.UTF-8',
           'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE':'1', 'PYTHONNOUSERSITE':'1'}
    command = ['/usr/bin/sandbox-exec', '-p', policy, *map(str, argv)]
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, close_fds=True,
                            input=input_text, text=True, capture_output=True,
                            timeout=timeout)

# Preparation and later mission

## Native activation gate

The CLI checks `require_native_activation` before destination preparation. Every native platform currently receives `activation unsupported`. There is no enable switch. The default runtime context also refuses direct helper use. The setup must remain inactive until a reviewed host adapter supplies every condition in runtime-contract.md. Neither Alex nor an agent can complete this by remembering to paste the right ID or by changing a JSON field.

The pure renderer prepares strings for testing; it does not create a chat or authenticate an identity. The separate fixture host materializes those strings under a disposable root with a host-created synthetic identity. It creates no mission, controller, grant, credential or schedule. It writes exclusively, retains an incomplete marker until the binding is written, refuses nonempty/nested homes and validates source hashes. Fixture output is marked `FIXTURE_ONLY_NATIVE_UNSUPPORTED`.

## Intended supported-host experience

1. Alex manually creates an empty operating folder and opens its first chat.
2. That chat invokes setup. The host authenticates its current identity directly and makes it Director; no second Director is created.
3. Fresh state has zero missions, controllers, approvals, account bindings and schedules. No mission is needed to initialize the home.
4. Alex assigns the mission afterward. The Director keeps bookkeeping here and records the actual target in PROJECT. It can work on a new project or an existing external repo. Read and preserve target instructions and current ownership; do not install the team in that repo.
5. The host grants only assigned paths/resources and creates fresh controller identities under this team. Every play names outcome, acceptance, current authority, allowed resource scope and exact local Conductor path.
6. The native adapter must prove delivery, return, acceptance and recovery. A queued event alone is not observed processing. One scoped schedule may be created only on explicit request, through host-enforced ownership.

This sequence is preserved as the contract for the missing native adapter, not represented as observed behavior.

## Local operations

Bookkeeping calls require trusted host context. They reject foreign state and return addresses, use anchored no-follow operations, and keep logs local even when PROJECT is external. Authorizations require an existing strict record tied to current mission/play/controller/generation/outcome/scope and a digest supplied by the trusted authority owner. Self-authored matching ledger hashes are insufficient.

The host must isolate arbitrary worker code from team state, immutable helpers, authority registry, credentials and other teams. Only its fixed privileged helper entrypoints receive local bookkeeping access. Shared cards and standards may be mounted read-only; recurring fixes go into local maintainer proposals.

## Recovery

Do not steal old locks by age. Ledger failure retains the write lock; use the same host-authorized restore path with the active backup. Graph and acceptance operations serialize on a stable lock. An interrupted acceptance leaves a pending journal; the next acceptance restores graph and log together before retry, while independent graph edits refuse to overwrite unresolved acceptance. Interrupted guard transitions remain unresolved and block replay/rotation. Never recover recipients or schedules outside the host's team registry.

A moved home or changed owner needs a separately reviewed transfer. No path override, symbolic link, mutable environment identity or copied approval is a valid transfer. The current native gate does not offer a transfer API.

# Runtime contract and supported-platform limits

## Supported proof scope

Only the isolated synthetic macOS subprocess reference host has been exercised. The candidate runner installs Seatbelt restrictions on every command and descendant it launches, clears ambient environment, closes inherited descriptors, denies network, Mach service lookup/registration, signaling and process inspection, and restricts data reads/writes to host-selected paths. Useful external project work remains available.

Literal ancestor-directory reads are needed for macOS startup and anchored descriptor walks. They disclose directory entry names at those ancestors; they do not permit reading private sibling file contents. This edition does not promise zero filesystem-name visibility.

The trusted host remains outside its workers' sandbox. It owns identity, authority, code fingerprints, resource leases and recipients. Only fixed helper commands receive bookkeeping writes; arbitrary code receives assigned project writes only. Helper code, bindings, approval registries and broad credentials must not be worker-writable. For the fixture host these registries are memory owned by the trusted test driver, not files reachable by workers. They are not a durable native service or a cross-machine resource authority.

The fixture launcher supplies context in a supervisor-created fixed helper process. JSON sent from an untrusted worker is not an authentication mechanism. Running that launcher directly outside its host boundary provides no supported identity guarantee. Standalone production helpers refuse context; native activation remains disabled in code.

## Current native platforms

Codex desktop, Claude Code, Claude app and Cursor activation are **unsupported in this revision**. Only Codex's exposed local surface and current official docs were investigated; no claim is made to have tested a negative action on the other platforms. The gate refuses them until each has an actual reviewed adapter. The current Codex chat uses broad host permissions. Codex command profiles do not govern its native apps/connectors/MCP/browser/computer actions. This script cannot retroactively constrain those tools.

Sources: [Codex permissions](https://developers.openai.com/codex/permissions/), [App Server](https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server/), [MCP configuration](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/), [scheduled tasks](https://developers.openai.com/codex/app/automations/). See the enclosing PLATFORM-EVIDENCE.md for actual calls, source versions and exact limits. No security configuration was changed.

## Mandatory native prerequisites

A supported adapter must establish all of these before setup, every resume and every scheduled turn:

1. Host-authenticated current chat identity and membership, retained outside agent-controlled inputs. The first manually opened chat becomes Director. A title, environment variable, file, argument or matching ID string is insufficient.
2. Enforced restrictions across **every exposed tool**: original/private team state and session/credential stores inaccessible; immutable shared standards readable only as assigned; explicit external project roots writable; broad op/Composio credentials and foreign native/server sockets absent. No direct native or shell bypass around the broker remains exposed.
3. One authoritative owner for each canonical provider/account/resource and each filesystem target, with overlap refusal. Scope aliases must resolve to the same resource; a new key or independent per-team registry cannot erase a conflict. Provider-side scopes or a trusted broker must enforce the account boundary.

## File and concurrency controls

safe_io pins the team-home directory descriptor, walks components using no-follow directory opens and checks actual opened regular files for ownership and a single link. A fully privileged hostile host is outside the supported threat boundary.

Atomic files use same-directory temporary files, fsync, and descriptor-relative replace/link operations. Exclusive create permits one winner. Stable flock files are not deleted while concurrent processes might reference them. Ledger backup/verify/restore is serialized; the logical write lock persists across commands and is never taken over by age. This lock still assumes the trusted host serializes that Director's multi-command edit session; a worker has no direct ledger write permission.

Graph and acceptance writes share a transaction lock. Acceptance journals both originals before graph/log changes. It reports success after both writes; a pending journal causes recovery before the next acceptance. This does not make separate later ledger updates one atomic operation, or deduplicate all repeated human acceptance requests. ## API contract

`Registry.create(private_root, native_data_roots=())` initializes an existing canonical, owner-only, empty directory. Explicit trusted installation action only. `Registry.open(private_root)` recovers an existing registry and refuses missing files, altered checksums, schema drift, failed integrity/FK checks, wrong owners/permissions, links and live database inode replacement. Never call `create` as a fallback to failed recovery; never reconstruct membership/approvals from worker-readable bindings. Missing durable authority stops the host.

`reserve_host_roots(paths)` adds canonical private/native/temp directories for each further client to the same registry and refuses overlaps with existing team/project roots. All teams on one trusted host must share this single registry; per-team registries cannot prove cross-team ownership exclusion. Registry creation and this reservation remain trusted parent-only operations.

`register_team(team_id, team_home, director_id)` takes the first Director ID from a trusted native creation response, and an existing canonical manually empty home. It pins the home device/inode and creates no controller, mission, project, authorization or lease. The separate parent renderer writes setup files after registration. Homes cannot overlap existing homes, assigned projects, private registry or supplied native data roots.

`register_controller(team_id, native_id, mission_id, generation)` takes a fresh native creation response from the trusted parent. IDs are globally unique and never reusable after revocation. Generation is a positive integer strictly greater than the prior generation for that team/mission. A newer generation revokes old controller membership and current approvals while retaining history. This method performs no native thread creation and must never be exposed to a worker.

`assign_project(team_id, path, mission_id)` is a trusted operator assignment after setup. The parent may explicitly create the project first; the registry only accepts existing canonical directories with no symlink component and pins device/inode. It refuses overlap with any team home, registry/native-data roots or another team's project. It conservatively reserves overlapping roots exclusively to one mission even within the same team. Claims remain durable through revocation; there is no automatic reassignment/release path in this bounded version.

`assigned_projects(actor)` returns sorted pinned canonical path strings for active registered actors. The Director receives the team's assigned roots for read-only use; a controller receives only its bound mission's roots. The broker must additionally require current authorization plus guard claim/state before any worker write. This query grants no write permission by itself.

`approve(team_id, ref, record)` is available only to the trusted human/operator host action. It validates team, Director, active controller, mission, generation, next play, outcome hash and scope; stores the approved exact record bytes/digest and a canonical resource lease; and returns `bytes`. The parent writes these exact bytes at `ref`, under that team's `mission-graphs` directory. It never writes authorization into a worker-writable folder by itself. Each reference is immutable and used once; use a fresh reference for every approval. A new approval deactivates earlier approvals for that mission without deleting them. Failed writing after approval leaves an unusable missing record and cannot create authority from worker data.

The record schema is the existing `independent-team-authorization/v1` helper contract. The only scope supported is exactly:

```json
{"action":"update","provider":"local-filesystem","account":"uid:<actual host uid>","resource_type":"project","resource":"<canonical project path assigned to this controller mission>"}
```

No external account/provider, composite scope, schedule or invented mock capability is accepted. The canonical resource key uses the existing `controller-resource-key/v1` digest shape, Unicode NFC normalization, casefolded provider/resource type, account and target. It has no team salt. Conflicting grants serialize under a private lock and SQLite transaction; durable unique claims permit one owner. Project overlap conflicts are also checked inside that transaction.

`context(actor)` returns `team_id`, `team_home`, `role`, `thread_id`, `director_thread_id`, `authorizations` (absolute reference → exact SHA256 digest) and `resource_leases` (canonical key list). Controllers see only active approvals for their own identity/current generation and leases within their assigned mission roots. Director sees the team's current approvals. Context is host-provided subprocess input, never accepted from worker arguments or environment.

`check_authorization(actor, ref, raw)` requires the current context-approved digest of the exact bytes. Missing, altered, revoked, superseded or wrong-controller records fail closed. The existing helper additionally validates mission/play/outcome/scope hashes against ledger state; parent broker owns its pending-claim/completed/uncertain fences.

`recipient_check(actor, target, operation)` accepts only owned, active registered same-team actors for `send`, `queue`, `resume`, `recover`. Parent must invoke the native route with this checked target only. Unknown/foreign/revoked recipients have no arbitrary-native-target fallback. All schedules/recurrence and unknown operations are explicitly refused; no scheduling is created.

`revoke_actor(actor)` retains membership rows but makes the actor and its approvals inactive. Revoking the Director closes the entire team and its approvals; new controllers/projects/approvals are then refused. `revoke_authorization(ref)` deactivates but preserves the historical digest/record. No destructive history deletion or reactivation API exists.

All operations raise `AuthorityError` for rejection. Database commits followed by interrupted seal writes deliberately cause fail-closed recovery rather than reconstructing authority. Multi-step native thread creation plus registration must be coordinated by the parent; unregistered partially-created threads acquire no authority.

Behavioral suite: 22 tests passed on macOS on 2026-10-03. Tests first failed because the implementation was absent; later regression tests exposed missing-path exception handling and Director revocation before those were repaired. Tests use isolated temporary folders and synthetic IDs only. See `authority-tests/receipt.txt` in the task's scratch host-layer folder for the recorded fresh run. The worker canary test calls the existing production `restricted_runtime.run`, denies reading/writing both SQLite registry and canary, and successfully writes its assigned external project. # Restricted native client

Local component for a trusted parent host; stock desktop integration is unproven. It does not activate the reusable Director setup, authenticate the existing desktop chat, own an authority registry, render roles, manage missions or connect a provider.

## Trusted parent API

`NativeClient(state_dir=..., temp_dir=..., operating_home=..., relay_url="http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1", model=..., dynamic_tools=[...], tool_handler=..., timeout=30, restorable_thread_ids=())`

All constructor values come from the protected parent, never tool arguments or worker files. The three directories must already exist, be canonical, owned by the host user and separate. Their device/inode identities are pinned when the client is constructed and all three are revalidated before each launch. State/temp must not be group/world writable. The parent must use dedicated private roots excluded from every worker; these ownership/mode checks alone cannot isolate unrestricted processes with the same UID. The native engine can read operating_home and can write only state/temp plus the establis

hed public/system exceptions. The model relay must be an already configured trusted host dependency at exactly the accepted loopback address. Credentials and provider connections are outside this client.

- `initialize()` launches bundled app-server under the proven OS profile, then initializes private stdio. Returns the native initialize result.
- `start_thread(base_instructions="", developer_instructions="")` returns native thread/start result and binds its real native ID. Starts with `environments=[]` and host-provided dynamic tools.
- `turn(thread_id, text)` starts with `environments=[]`, dispatches matching dynamic callbacks and returns the exact matching successful `turn/completed` parameters. Timeout, malformed stdio and failed active turn stop the server. Unrelated notifications remain in `events` and cannot complete the active turn.

- `resume(thread_id)` permits only IDs created on this object or explicitly granted through `restorable_thread_ids`. Native resumed ID must match. The restoring parent must derive that grant from its intact protected registry and matching native-state root. The grant itself is not actor/model authentication. There is no arbitrary resume fallback.
- `stop()` waits for server termination, closes private transport/logs and releases the state lock; calling again is safe. Restarting the same object reacquires the lock and retains its bound set.
- `pid` exposes the live server process ID or None. `events` records every consumed native message for host diagnostics; parent should archive/drain it at safe turn boundaries to limit memory.

Handler receives immutable `ToolCall(thread_id, turn_id, call_id, tool, arguments)` made from server stdout only. It returns `{"contentItems": [{"type": "inputText", "text": "..."}], "success": true}` (or false). Handler validates argument schema, authority, resource grants and generation fence before doing work. Actor fields inside arguments cannot change the ToolCall identity. Missing/mismatched callback identity, unknown tools and unexpected native UI/tool requests are denied. Handler failure returns a generic denied result. One synchronous caller owns each client; handler must not reenter it.

Config, stderr and lock are opened relative to the checked state-directory descriptor with symlink, hardlink, nonregular-file, owner and group/world-writable checks. Config is written through an exclusive checked temporary file and atomically replaced within that descriptor. No global safe_io bind is used. A lock identity is retained across restarts on the same object. A stable `.native-host.lock` inode holds an exclusive nonblocking process lock before any state/config write or native launch. A second live client on that root refuses. No lock stealing by age or unlinking occurs. Parent FDs are not inherited by native children. This is local ownership of a state root, not a durable authority registry or proven supervisor-crash recovery.

## Boundary and tests

Uses the bundled ChatGPT native executable and existing restricted_runtime profile without changing either. Native direct apps/MCP/browser/shell/unified-exec/multiagent/goals routes are disabled; unexpected requests have no native UI fallback. The only network exception is the exact local relay port. Additional proven OS exceptions are self-only process information, opendirectoryd.libinfo, and public bundle metadata/passwd. Preferences/keychain IPC remains denied.

Run `python3 -m unittest discover -v` from this directory. Scripted Responses relay exists only in the test module. Tests exercise real native start/turn/dynamic dispatch, true callback/completion identity, hostile unregistered builtin refusal, denied native UI route, model actor arguments, unrelated completion handling, malformed callback denial, stop/restart/resume, fresh-client restore with explicit trusted grants, missing-grant refusal, second state owner refusal and clean shutdown. No live model/account is used. Native `request_user_input` is offered but the default-mode router itself returns unavailable; the broker s

eparately tests deny-default native UI requests.

Native persistence observation: thread/start alone does not guarantee a resumable rollout. The fresh-client restoration test completes a turn before stopping. Native no-rollout failures remain errors, not synthetic restoration receipts.

The narrow accepted probe remains the source for full OS canary/network/foreign-state denial evidence. These client tests do not repeat that study or prove all future native tool versions, stock desktop interception or complete team behavior. Primary integration and acceptance are still required. No project-wide lint/typecheck is configured in this standalone component; all local tests run via unittest discovery.

Focused review repair on 2026-10-03 reproduced and corrected foreign-file truncation through config links, redirected stderr through links, hardlinked lock acceptance, replaced directory roots and a turn/start timeout leaving the server live. The start request is now inside the turn failure-stop boundary. Seven focused regressions plus the seven existing native component tests passed together: 14 tests, 3.156 seconds. See `SECURITY-REPAIR-RECEIPT.md`. Poison-path regressions suppress only actual process launch, and assert real parent filesystem effects; the timeout regression injects a protocol timeout but observes termination of a real harmless child process. The existing component tests still exercise the actual shipped native server and scripted local relay. These focused cases do not prove a supervisor crash recovery implementation or filesystem safety against an unrestricted same-UID process racing root renames. Native/worker OS exclusion is required.

# Reproduce the native component probe

This is a characterization harness with a scripted local model, not a Director installation or a live-model launcher. It uses the actual engine bundled with the local desktop app. All native runtime state is created under the provided scratch directory. The main user's native state, model credentials, original chats and installed setup are not used.

Run the copied harness with an existing disposable scratch directory:

```sh
python3 native_probe.py --scratch /absolute/path/to/existing/disposable/scratch
```

The executable and revision-03 `restricted_runtime.py` locations are pinned in the harness. It requires macOS, `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`, the reviewed local candidate runtime and the bundled Codex engine. It does not install dependencies. Each run creates a fresh `probe-<timestamp>` folder and stops its own native server processes and local scripted-model server before returning. Exit zero means its listed checks passed; it does not enable the setup skill's native gate.

Inspect `observations.json` for the real native events, model requests, per-call outputs, worker results and assertions. The only upstream model endpoint is the test's one loopback port. Native command workers cannot contact that port. No model-provider credentials are sent. The native chat is persisted inside the disposable native data directory so the test can restart the process and resume the same chat.

The allowed native model tools are the bounded `probe_worker` and the native user-input tool. Actual command work happens in a stricter subprocess boundary with fixed assigned roots. Unexpected client-side native requests are refused. Unsupported engine calls are deliberately generated by the scripted model and must be refused by the engine itself.

Read STATUS.md before interpreting results. The harness does not implement a durable supervisor, multiple-team/account arbitration, the actual Director/controller role workflow, owned messaging/scheduling or the first-existing-desktop-chat connection. Do not use the probe's in-memory registry as production authority. Do not start a real model or broaden a permission because this probe passes.

The installed desktop application is `/Applications/ChatGPT.app`, bundle `com.openai.codex`, version 26.930.21537 (12776). Its shipped engine is Codex CLI 0.159.0-alpha.12.1. The previous investigation found the separately installed CLI 0.160.0 but missed this application name; these versions are distinct.

The shipped native app server ran in a disposable macOS Seatbelt boundary. It created one real native chat, delivered a dynamic tool call with the server's actual thread and turn IDs, accepted the returned result, persisted that chat, and resumed the same identity after the server process restarted. The test driver retains ownership outside the command worker. There is no editable identity string used as authentication.

The model endpoint is a **local scripted Responses test double**. It deliberately emits permitted and hostile tool calls. The engine, its tool selection and dispatch, native thread IDs, file operations and operating-system denials are real. No OpenAI model request, API credential or real customer/service action was used. This proves engine behavior under controlled model output, not model reasoning or a live Director/controller workflow.

The current primary run has 25 passing checks and no failing checks. Raw evidence is `probe-1791037333855902000/observations.json`; the compact result is `native-component-summary.json`.

- A tool reached through actual native dispatch wrote and read a disposable external project file.
- The command worker was denied foreign dummy-credential reads/writes, native authority/config reads, direct team-state writes and network access, including access to the local model endpoint.
- A caller identity inserted into tool arguments was refused before running a worker command.
- The engine's offered tools were limited to the bounded dynamic worker and native user-input tool. Shell, patch, image, subagent, native messaging, scheduling and MCP resource bypass calls emitted by the scripted model were refused by native dispatch.
- Restarting the engine and resuming the same native chat retained the restricted catalog. Useful work still succeeded and a foreign read was still denied.
- The foreign canary retained its original content. Both native server processes were stopped after the test.

These are 25 assertions over a small native-component experiment. They are not 25 complete isolation requirements, and they do not replace the previous 89-case candidate suite.

## Startup failures and correction

All failed attempts remain evidence. The first profile used a numeric IP where Seatbelt requires `localhost`. The next attempt crashed because native macOS logging needs its own process identifier. A self-only process-information exception fixed that crash without enabling foreign-process inspection.

Native configuration then refused startup with `Failed to synchronize managed preferences`. Exact preference-service exceptions did not fix it and were removed. A diagnostic attempt with exact public bundle metadata, the public passwd file and a disposable process home still failed. The kernel log identified denied `com.apple.system.opendirectoryd.libinfo` lookups; the current UID is not represented in the public passwd file. The bundled native minimal policy independently permits this ordinary user-name lookup. Allowing that one service resolved startup. **Preference services, keychain services and general Mach access remain denied.**

The native process can read its executable, exact public bundle metadata, public system runtime, assigned test paths and its isolated native data. It can write only its own disposable data/temp roots. It can contact only the one exact loopback port for the scripted model. Directory-entry visibility at necessary ancestor paths and ordinary UID/name lookup are acknowledged; the design does not promise zero machine metadata visibility.

Commands run by the bounded tool receive the earlier candidate's stricter subprocess boundary, including complete Mach and network denial, scrubbed environment and no inherited extra file descriptors. They do not inherit the native engine's data directory or model endpoint access.

Read-only inspection found that the desktop can update a chat's command permissions and select its own MCP tools internally. It did not establish a supported external hook for attaching this trusted broker to an already-created desktop chat across all tools. Internal Electron handlers are not a supported integration contract. The bundled protocol's existing-chat settings update has no tool-interceptor or dynamic-tool registration field.

The explicit user experience is manual folder creation, its first chat invoking setup and becoming Director, mission assignment afterward, and work in a new or existing external project. ## Exposed API limits

The current tool catalog exposes no tool for changing this chat's native tool catalog, installing an interception policy, binding an external trusted identity provider, or enforcing a team-scoped native recipient ACL. `request_permissions` can request additional command filesystem/network permissions; it does not revoke all tool authority. Plugin management permissions are global/plugin-level choices, not chat/team ownership scopes. The thread creation/handoff tools do not expose a per-chat tool policy or trusted-adapter field. No such tools were invoked.

Standalone CLI help provides `app-server proxy --sock` and authenticated app-server transports; proxying bytes to a running server does not itself establish a broker or authorization. Daemon management can start/restart/enable remote control, but those are environment/service mutations and were not invoked.

The primary's generated standalone 0.160.0 schema adds useful detail, but should be regenerated with the bundled binary before desktop compatibility claims:

- `ThreadSettingsUpdateParams` can replace `disabledPluginIds`, select `permissions`, or override `sandboxPolicy` / `cwd`; it has no `dynamicTools`, `config`, immutable caller-binding or tool-interceptor property.
- `ThreadResumeParams` accepts `config`, permission roots and thread identity; it has no `dynamicTools` field.
- `ThreadStartParams` accepts `dynamicTools`, `config`, `permissions`, runtime roots and server-created thread identity.
Smallest justified probe and UX boundary

A config map is not proof that every tool route can be disabled, that settings cannot be changed by the agent, or that the desktop cannot reintroduce its tools during resume. Each needs separate host evidence. Private renderer IPC handlers or editing packaged Electron code would be unsupported implementation work, not an established supported adapter route.

## Smallest justified probe and UX boundary

A disposable instance of the **bundled native app server** can be hosted by a trusted controller, in a separately restricted operating environment, with only explicitly selected broker tools. Its own server-created thread IDs can be retained outside workers. A scripted local model endpoint can prove actual native dispatch without provider credentials or model spending. This is a viable native-component experiment. It is **not** fulfillment of the existing first desktop chat requirement.
Smallest justified probe and UX boundary

The required missing bridge is a vendor-supported way for the already-created first desktop chat to (1) authenticate its own identity to the broker, (2) use only that broker's allowed engine/native/app/browser/service routes, and (3) retain that enforcement on resume/queue/wake while still displaying and operating as the same Director chat. Standalone server connection authentication, editable environment IDs and instruction-only tool prohibitions cannot supply that bridge.

A sandbox applied only to the local helper leaves desktop tool dispatch untouched. A sandbox around an unrelated standalone server likewise does not mediate the original desktop conversation. Sandboxing/replacing the entire current desktop app would affect other chats and still needs a supported deployment/control contract; it was not attempted or authorized here.
